note: The Round Trip table: ONE ROW PER BRIEF STEP FIELD (kogaki#1013/#1014).
`field` names the Brief Step field the Reverse Outline side is read from, under
the Brief's own name and definition. It replaces the translation column, which was a
TRANSLATION COLUMN between the Brief and a second schema for the same
information — that schema is deleted, so what the column translated between no
longer has two sides. Where `field` and `declared_block` read the same, that is
the round trip: the same field, forward and reverse.
THE HYGIENE AND MOVE ROWS ARE GONE, and their removal is the ruling rather than
a trim (owner, 2026-09-09). Prose hygiene is not part of Reverse Outlining: a
reader cannot infer the source a structure was produced from, and being able to
would be abnormal. So exemplar-leak, packet-wording, term-before-introduction
and restates-earlier-step left the table. move-contract left with them because
the Move is not in the Reverse Outline at all — supplying the candidates would
make the outcome ride on supplied information, and the Move's effect is carried
by the reader states, which ARE compared. Whether any of the five survives as a
realization-time lint in `draft` is a separate question for the owner.
`register-tests` LEFT THE TABLE FOR THE SAME REASON, one ruling later
(owner, 2026-09-11). It was the last prose lint standing: its declared side
was the Packet's write-instruction paragraph and its reverse side was the
passage itself, so no Reverse Outline field was involved at all. In the
first full run it failed on seven of eight Steps, every time on "one
relation per sentence", and sent nothing to correction -- a best-effort row
that fires on almost every Step reports the register of the prose, not a
reconstruction gap. Whether register lints return at realization time inside
`draft` stays the open question the paragraph above already records; it is
the same question for this row.
AND `already-knows` GAINS A `when_declared_absent` ARM in the same act. Its
declared side is the Packet's `already knows` list, which is EMPTY for the
first Step of every article by construction, and the pair was rendered
anyway: the model was asked whether the passage re-introduced a term the
reader already knew, over a list of no terms, and returned `fails` with a
reason stating the opposite -- that the passage introduces both terms for
the first time. `grounds` and `introduces` already carry such an arm and
reach the same runtime branch, so this is one table entry and no second
mechanism.
`concession` is the ONE row whose field is a Packet clause rather than a Brief
field, and it is declared as such: the Packet's write instruction requires a
loss to be conceded in the prose, so a conceded softening is told from a silent
one.
The comparison's ITEM TABLE, fixed in the Harness (kogaki#872).
WHICH PACKET INFORMATION MUST BE RECONSTRUCTIBLE IS DECIDED ONCE, HERE, per
item class — and the judging model never assigns one. It answers one
question about one pair and returns one of three tokens. src/review-draft.mjs
READS this file rather than restating it, the same arrangement
one edit and never a two-copy divergence.
`class` IS THE CONSEQUENCE, not a severity. A Step is sent to correction only
on a `fails` in a PRESERVED item; a best-effort fail rides along when that
Step is re-realized anyway. There is no score, no ranking and no aggregate —
the three tokens are the whole vocabulary, and `cannot-decide` is never
rounded to either neighbour.
`mode` IS WHO DECIDES, and it is the half that keeps the model out of the
mechanical items:
- `mechanical` — the Harness decides from string facts about the Draft and
the Packet. NO join Packet is rendered and no model call is made.
- `judged`     — the Harness renders one join Packet (the declared line,
the outlined line, the quoted span, one question) and records the
verdict that comes back.
- `paired`     — the Harness pairs the outlined entries against the
declared ones MECHANICALLY; an entry that pairs with nothing is decided
here, by name, with no model call, and the paired set is then judged.
This is the one hybrid, and it exists because `widened` is a fact about
the pairing rather than a reading of it.
`declared_block` names the Packet block the declared side is read from, and
src/review-draft.mjs refuses BY NAME when a Packet carries no such block —
a missing block is a PACKET GAP filed against src/packet-template.md, per
the owner's 2026-09-04 closed-input ruling, and never something the
comparison works around.
NOT COMPARED, enumerated so a reader can tell a boundary from a hole:
rationale, materials, reader_state_before, and the thesis and reader target
per Step. The article level is the cold reader's (kogaki#873).
THE FIGURE HALF IS BACK, RESTATED AGAINST THE RECORD'S OWN FIELDS
(kogaki#1018). It left this table at kogaki#1014 under a recorded decline: its
five rows read a reverse side out of the second schema that act deleted, and
the Blind Reader returns a Brief Step block, which carries no such field.
WHAT REPLACED IT IS THE PASSAGE'S OWN RULE, ONE ARTIFACT DOWN. A passage is
written from a Brief Step, so its Reverse Outline is a Brief Step block; a
figure is written from its RECORD, so its Reverse Outline is a block in the
fields src/figure-schema.json declares. There is no second schema at either
level, which is the property kogaki#1014 landed and this is that property for
the figure.
THE DISPOSITION RULE IS THE SAME RULE. `element`, `caption` and `position` are
reconstructible and COMPARED -- a reader who met the rendered block can say
each of them. `kind`, `relations` and `emphasis` are not reconstructible and
are REFUSED rather than merely unasked: the kind and the relations are the
Move form's, and a reader cannot infer the form a structure was produced from.
IT IS ITS OWN FENCE AND ITS OWN FILE. `figure` IS a Brief Step field and is
declared not reconstructible, so a `figure:` line inside the passage's outline
stays refused; one file per vocabulary is what keeps either reading from
acquiring a key belonging to the other.
`figure_only: true` marks a row that exists only for a Step whose trace entry
carries a figure. On a Step without one the row is not evaluated, not rendered
and NOT LOGGED -- a vacuous `holds` for every figureless Step would put a
figure line in a Draft that has no figure. `record_field` is to the figure
record what `declared_block` is to the Packet, and `figure_field` names the
line read back out of the figure's own Reverse Outline. A row naming both
`field` and `figure_field` is refused: that pair would be a translation
between the Brief's names and the record's, which is the column this chain
removed.
NOW COMPARED, and enumerated so a reader can tell a boundary from a hole:
the figure's elements, its caption, its element-to-ground binding, its reading
against the prose, and its position -- five rows, three preserved and two best-effort, on the same three verdicts and the same consequence rule.
THE PACKET'S LAYOUT IS DATA, not a literal in the runtime (kogaki#872).
src/review-draft.mjs reads a declared block by its KIND, and every label,
heading and fixed instruction sentence the reader keys on lives here. Two
things follow, and the second is the reason:
- amending src/packet-template.md is one edit here and never a hunt
through the comparison for a string that used to match;
- the runtime carries no literal that HAPPENS to equal a field name
somewhere else. `grounds`, `purpose` and `reader_state_after` are
each a Packet label AND an item id AND (for two of them) an outlined
record field, and a runtime spelling them out cannot be told apart
from one restating the table or the schema. A synonym in a join key
is the same defect as a divergence.
`after_words` is the template's own fixed instruction paragraph, matched
as a WORD SEQUENCE so a rewrap — which changes nothing — does not silently
hand the instruction back as the block's value.

move_excerpt.heading: An exemplar of this Move — FORM ONLY
move_excerpt.after_words: Read it for the form of the movement and nothing else.

section_placement.heading: The Section this Step sits in
section_placement.after_words: one, and the line below says which. Where it continues, the heading is already on the page and you are writing further into it: do not restate the heading's claim, and do not open a new subject.

note: THE SECOND PASS'S BOUND IS DATA, for the reason the packet_blocks
note gives one block down (kogaki#874). `check` re-judges the
corrected Steps' own items, the CONTINUITY items on the Step
immediately after each correction, and every mechanical item over
the whole Draft -- and the runtime names none of those ids, because
an item id spelled out in the runtime cannot be told from one
restating this table.
`successor_items` IS ONE id, and it was two (kogaki#1014). The issue
named two properties the successor carries -- `reader_state_before`
continuity and `restates`. The first is `already-knows`: no STEP item
reads the Packet's `reader_state_before` slot, and the block carrying
the reader's INCOMING state on the Step side is `already_knows`. The
second was `restates-earlier-step`, and that row left the table with
the hygiene rows -- a reader cannot infer the source a structure was
produced from -- so the property has no item to be re-checked on. It is
recorded here rather than dropped silently: the successor arm now
re-checks incoming-state continuity alone, and whether the restates
property returns as a realization-time lint in `draft` is the separate
question that removal left open.
NARROWED AT kogaki#873, which declares a reader for that block. This
clause read `this table declares NO reader for it`, flatly, and the
Section pair `section-belief-before` now reads exactly it. The
argument above is untouched -- it was always about which STEP item
carries incoming-state continuity -- and the sentence is narrowed to
what it was arguing rather than left standing as a false fact about
the table.
`drift_blocks` are the Packet blocks the drift measure reports
verbatim overlap against -- the ground and state lines. Same
arrangement, same reason.
THE FIGURE ROWS ARE BACK IN THE TABLE (kogaki#1018) AND STILL ADD NO ARM
HERE. They added none while they were here before, they removed none by
leaving, and they add none returning: the second pass's arms are the
corrected Steps' own items, the successor's continuity item and every
mechanical item, and a figure row is reached by whichever of those its
Step is in. `figure-element-ground` is mechanical, so it is in the third
arm over the whole Draft; the judged figure rows are in the first on a
corrected Step exactly as that Step's other rows are. NO FIGURE ROW IS A
SUCCESSOR ITEM: a correction moves the prose the NEXT Step continues
from, and it moves no figure.
Thresholds are INPUTS TO THE HARNESS AND NEVER OUTPUT. No emitted line
carries one — a comparison line renders line numbers and nothing else
numeric, so a reader cannot mistake a tuning constant for evidence.
THE COLD READER'S PAIRING TABLE, fixed in the Harness (kogaki#873).
A Section declares exactly ONE thing in the Brief: its heading, the
promise that the question changes here (DESIGN.md 2.1). Its reader path
is derivable from the trace and the Packets -- the first Step's
`reader_state_before` and the last Step's `reader_state_after` -- so NO
SECTION-LEVEL STEP IS MINTED. One would be a second authoring seat on
structure, and this table exists so that none is needed.
The cold reader reads the BODY ONLY: frontmatter stripped, no Packet
content. After each Section it records the question that Section put to
it and where the Section left it; at the end it records the article's
thesis. The pairs below are what the Harness lays those entries against,
and `class` is the CONSEQUENCE exactly as it is for the Step items. The
verdict vocabulary is the same three tokens, shared rather than
re-declared: `cannot-decide` is not rounded here either.
THE ENTRY'S FIELD NAMES ARE THE BRIEF'S OWN (kogaki#1014). They were
`question`, `belief` and `claim` -- a third vocabulary for what the Brief
already names `Opening question`, `Reader target` and the thesis, and a
name nobody else uses is the same drift one carrier over as the deleted
Reverse Outline was. So the cold reader answers in `opening_question`,
`reader_target` and `thesis`, and the Harness lays them against the
declared sides it already read. WHAT EACH PAIR COMPARES IS UNCHANGED:
this is a renaming of the reader's own answer sheet, not a new item, not
a new declared side and not a new consequence.
THE NAMES APPLY PER SECTION AND ONCE AT THE END, which is what the Brief
does with them too: `Opening question` is the question put to a reader
standing somewhere, and a Section is exactly the unit where that question
changes; `Reader target` is where they are left, and a Section leaves
them somewhere on the way to where the article does.
WHAT DIFFERS IS WHERE A FAIL GOES. ReviewDraft corrects at Step
granularity only, so a Section fail either LOCALIZES to a Step or routes
UPSTREAM to the Brief as residue. Which pairs exist and what each costs
are this table's; the routing rules are the runtime's.
`declared.from` names WHERE the declared side is read: `section_title`
from the trace, `first_step`/`last_step` from that Step's own Packet,
`any_packet` for a block every Packet carries identically because it is
a fixed point of the whole article. `reverse.from` names which ledger
entry answers: this Section's, the previous Section's, or the final
claim.
`vacuous_when` is how an item that asks about ONE Section says so, rather
than the runtime knowing which items are special. It is the ONLY key that
decides it: a companion `binds` was declared here at first and read
nowhere, so a later row whose two keys disagreed would have bound by one
and read as binding by the other -- the two-copy divergence the
packet_blocks note argues against, grown inside the table that argues it
(PR #930 round 1). Which Section an item binds on is readable from its
`vacuous_when` and is stated again in its `vacuous_sentence`, for the
reader rather than for the runtime.
A vacuous pair is decided by the Harness with the table's own sentence and
costs no model call -- it is not skipped, because a skipped pair and a
pair that held are the same silence to a reader.
`localizing_item` is the STEP item a Section fail localizes on when no
Step in the Section has failed a preserved item outright: the first Step
whose outlined reader state does not hold is where the Section's own
reader path came apart. It is named here rather than in the runtime for
the reason the packet_blocks note gives -- an item id spelled out in the
runtime cannot be told from one restating this table.

opening_question.prompt: the question this Section put to you, in one line

reader_target.prompt: where this Section left you — what you now believe, in one or two sentences

items.question: Does the question this reader says the Section answered match what its heading promises? Answer `fails` if the heading promises a different question, or promises one the reader did not find answered.

Do the declared reader state at the Section's end and what this reader now believes describe the same reader? Answer `fails` if a reader holding the outlined belief would not be in the declared state.

items.vacuous_sentence: this is the article's first Section, so no previous entry declares what the reader arrived believing
items.question: The reader arrives at this Section holding what the previous Section left them with. Does that match the state the Section's first Step declares it starts from? Answer `fails` if the Section starts from a reader who does not exist yet.

items.vacuous_sentence: the final claim is recorded once for the whole Draft and is paired at its last Section
items.question: Is what this reader says the article claimed the article's thesis? Answer `fails` if the outlined claim is a different claim, or a weaker or a wider one.

items.vacuous_sentence: this item asks what the first Section did with the opening question, and binds there only
items.question: After this first Section, is the article's opening question answered, or deliberately held open? Answer `fails` if the reader's belief neither answers it nor leaves it open -- if the question has simply been dropped.

when_declared_absent.sentence: this Step declares no grounds, so there is no declared ground for a claim to go beyond; what its claims assert is judged by the Step's other items, and `grounds-unused` names the absence

items.question: Does this outlined claim assert no more than the grounds this Step declares? Every declared ground is listed above; the claim need not correspond to any one of them in wording, and a claim may rest on several of them at once. Answer `fails` if the claim goes beyond what those grounds, taken together, license — in scope, in certainty, or in subject.

Does the state this passage assumes a reader arrives in match the state the Forward Artifact declares they arrive in? Answer `fails` where the passage assumes the reader already holds something the declared arriving state does not give them, or re-establishes something it does.
Do the declared reader state and the outlined one describe the same reader? Answer `fails` if a reader in the outlined state would not be in the declared one.

when_declared_absent.sentence: this Step's Packet says to introduce no term, so the question below quantifies over nothing, and a passage that introduces nothing carries no `introduces:` line to read against it

items.question: Is every term the Packet says to introduce here actually introduced in this passage — usable by the reader afterwards? Answer `fails` if a declared term is used without being made usable, or is not present at all.
Is any ground carried more weakly in the prose than the Packet declares it, with no concession outlined for it? Answer `fails` if a ground was softened silently.
Do the declared purpose and the outlined one name the same job for this Step? Answer `fails` if the passage is doing a different job.

when_declared_absent.sentence: this Step's Packet lists no term the reader already knows, so there is nothing for the passage to re-introduce and the question below quantifies over nothing

items.question: Does the passage re-introduce a term the reader already knows — explaining again what an earlier Step established? Answer `fails` if it does.

The Packet says whether this Step opens its Section or continues one. Where it CONTINUES, does the passage re-open the subject or restate the heading's claim? Answer `fails` if it does; answer `holds` where the Step opens its Section, since the item does not bind there.

Every element the record declares is above, with the wording it was given. Can a reader name each of them from the figure as it was rendered? Answer `fails` if an element the record declares is not among the ones the reader named. This asks about presence, never about how well an element is worded.

The declared side carries the record's caption and the state the Step says its reader is left in. Does what the reader holds after looking at the figure agree with both? Answer `fails` if it agrees with neither, or if it agrees with the caption while the caption and the Step's state pull apart.

Both sides here were read blind, from the passage and the figure the reader met beside it. Do the figure and the prose of this Step say the same thing? Answer `fails` if the figure asserts something the passage does not, or the other way about.

The declared side says whether the figure was designed to set the passage up or to discharge it, and the reverse side is where the reader says they met it. The figure's draft line numbers in the prose below say where it actually sits. Did the reader meet it where the prose needed it? Answer `fails` if the passage had already done the work the figure was meant to set up, or still needed the figure it had not yet been given.
